t: Find Consecutive Integers from a Data Stream
o: Design DataStream(value, k): consec(num) appends num and reports whether the last k parsed integers all equal value. Rather than storing the stream, note the answer only depends on the length of the current trailing run of `value`: increment it when num == value, reset to 0 otherwise, and return run ≥ k. In the example (value=4, k=3) the runs after each call are 1, 2, 3, 0 → false, false, true, false. O(1) per call, O(1) memory.
k: Only the trailing run length of `value` matters — no history storage needed.
consec is O(1): increment or reset a counter, compare with k.

a.i: Maintain cnt = length of the current suffix of identical-to-value numbers. On each consec call, cnt = cnt+1 if num == value else 0; return cnt >= k. This automatically handles the fewer-than-k-integers case since cnt can't reach k before k calls.
s: On consec(num): cnt = cnt + 1 if num == value else 0.

a.n: Approach 2: Bounded queue of recent values
a.i: Keep a deque holding the last k parsed numbers and a count of how many of them equal value. On each call push num (evicting the oldest when size exceeds k, decrementing the equality count if the evicted value matched), update the count for num, and return count == k. This generalizes verbatim to 'last k integers satisfy predicate P', whereas the counter trick only works for exact-equality predicates.
s: Maintain a deque of the last k numbers and a match counter.
Push num; if the deque exceeds k, pop the front and decrement the counter if it equaled value.
Increment the counter if num == value; return counter == k.
a.t: O(1) per call — amortized deque operations

w: Ship the counter solution — it is optimal and trivially correct. The queue version earns points in interviews as the extensible pattern (any sliding-window predicate). Pitfalls: returning true before k integers have arrived (the counter handles this implicitly; the queue checks size explicitly), and resetting the counter on any non-matching value. Follow-up: 'last k integers are all distinct' or 'non-decreasing' — switch to the windowed-statistics pattern.
